title: Microsoft Purview: exclude Microsoft 365 groups and target dynamic and non-mail-enabled security groups in sensitivity label policies
notes: claim 55: severity blocker on a rationale: impact rating lowered to minor; ratings are judgements and cannot hold a page
summary: Hold: policy ordering resolves conflicting settings, rather than choosing a single policy that applies to a user. The claim that admin time is the only new cost overlooks the licensing requirement for dynamic group membership. Users can also lose a policy through membership changes without an administrator retargeting it.

claims.claim: Publishing label policies determines which users see labels and receive label policy settings.
claims.quote:
When you publish the label policy to your chosen users:

- The policy settings are applied to these users

claims.where: controls[2].governs; Governance guidance: At rollout; Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: Policy order decides which label policy applies when several policies cover the same user.
claims.quote: You can include a user in multiple label policies, and the user gets all the sensitivity labels and settings from those policies. If there's a conflict in settings from multiple policies, the settings from the policy with the highest priority (highest order number) is applied.
claims.fix: Replace controls[2].governs with 'Which label policy settings win when assigned policies conflict'. Replace the At rollout ordering bullet with 'Review label policy order after adding exclusions: users receive labels from all assigned policies, and the highest-priority policy wins for each conflicting setting.' Replace 'which policy a user gets' in Risk assessment with 'which policy settings win when assigned policies conflict'. Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/sensitivity-labels#label-policy-priority-order-matters.

claims.claim: Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Information Protection > Publishing policies > Publish label > Assign admin units reaches administrative-unit scoping.
claims.quote: On the Label policies page, select Publish label ... On the Choose sensitivity labels to publish page, select the Choose sensitivity labels to publish link. ... For the Assign admin units
claims.fix: Expand the path to 'Solutions > Information Protection > Publishing policies > Publish label > Choose sensitivity labels to publish > Choose sensitivity labels to publish > Assign admin units'. The omitted selection identifies the labels being published rather than a different policy type. Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/create-sensitivity-labels.
